profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, at 165 Halsey Street in Newark, New Jersey, is one of the most significant carrier hotel and data center buildings in the New York metropolitan area. Built in 1912 as a Bamberger's department store and expanded twice by 1929, the fourteen story, 1.2 million square foot building sat vacant after Macy's closed the store in 1992 until developer Samuel Jemal recognized its sturdy floor loading and large open floor plates as well suited to telecommunications and data center use, beginning conversion in 1996. Documented tenants include Equinix, which operates its NY1 facility there and is separately profiled in this registry Equinix facility cluster, along with Level 3 Communications, Verizon Business, CenturyLink, BT Americas, Telecom Italia Sparkle, and Zayo Group; the building is also a landing point for the Apollo transatlantic submarine cable system and hosts multiple internet exchange points. Commercial data center directories including Baxtel, Inflect, and Cloudscene list an entity called Tishman Real Estate Services as associated with the building address, consistent with a property or facilities management role, but this was not corroborated in Wikipedia, AECOM own project page, or other primary sources, and is treated as an unverified directory level lead. The well documented Tishman corporate family split in 1976 into Tishman Speyer, Tishman Hotel and Realty LP, and a construction division later sold to AECOM in 2010, now AECOM Tishman; no source ties any of those named entities specifically to this address. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
The 165 Halsey Street building in Newark is a 1.2 million square foot converted department store built in 1912 that has operated as a carrier hotel and data center since 1996. Its floor loading capacity and large open floor plates were recognized as suited to data center use, and it now hosts multiple telecommunications carriers and internet exchange points. The building is a landing point for the Apollo transatlantic submarine cable system. No IT capacity figure is published for this facility.

The building's operator is listed as Tishman in commercial data center directories, but this association was not corroborated in primary sources and remains unverified; the Tishman corporate entities documented in public records are not specifically tied to this address. Equinix operates its NY1 facility within the building, and documented tenants include Level 3 Communications, Verizon Business, CenturyLink, BT Americas, Telecom Italia Sparkle, and Zayo Group.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 megawatts. This facility does not publish a capacity figure and therefore cannot be ranked within the state by megawatts. Its significance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from published specifications.
